title: Place Value to a Million (KS2)
subject: Maths
strapline: What each digit is worth, and reading big numbers.
facts: The value of a digit depends on its place in the number — this is place value.
Columns from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions.
In 3,482 the 3 is worth 3 thousands (3000), the 4 is 4 hundreds, the 8 is 8 tens, the 2 is 2 ones.
Zero is a place holder — it keeps other digits in the right column, as in 306 (no tens).
To multiply by 10, 100 or 1000, the digits move left by 1, 2 or 3 places.
To compare numbers, line up the columns and compare from the largest column first.
Rounding: look at the digit to the right — 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less rounds down.

quick_quiz.q: What is the value of the 7 in 47,200?

teacher_tips: Use place-value counters/columns so "moving left when ×10" is seen, not just told.
Stress zero as a placeholder — reading 3,004 correctly is a good check.
Read big numbers aloud in groups of three digits.
